Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১) What is the commonest symptom in a patient with carcinoma rectum?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The commonest symptom of carcinoma rectum is hematochezia (passage of fresh blood per rectum). Rectal tumors commonly ulcerate and bleed, producing bright red blood mixed with or coating the stool. Other symptoms include altered bowel habits, tenesmus, constipation, and a sensation of incomplete evacuation. Abdominal pain is less common in early rectal carcinoma and usually occurs with advanced disease or obstruction. Diarrhoea may occur due to altered bowel function but is not the most typical presentation. Constipation may occur but is usually a later feature. Therefore, among the given options, hematochezia is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Rectal carcinoma → hematochezia is a common presenting symptom

  • Other features → tenesmus, altered bowel habit, mucus discharge

  • Blood in rectal cancer → usually bright red

  • Left-sided colorectal cancers often present with bleeding and altered bowel habits

Exam Pearl:
Bright red blood per rectum in an adult = suspect carcinoma rectum until proven otherwise.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২) NSAIDs induced ulcers are best treated with ……?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are the preferred treatment for NSAID-induced peptic ulcers because they strongly suppress gastric acid secretion by irreversibly inhibiting the H⁺/K⁺ ATPase pump in gastric parietal cells. This promotes ulcer healing and reduces the risk of complications such as bleeding. Misoprostol, a prostaglandin analogue, is effective mainly for prevention of NSAID-induced ulcers, especially in high-risk patients, but its use is limited by adverse effects like diarrhea. H2 blockers and sucralfate are less effective than PPIs for NSAID-associated ulcers.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • NSAID ulcers → PPI is the treatment of choice

  • NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin synthesis by inhibiting COX enzymes

  • Misoprostol → prevents NSAID ulcers

  • PPI → promotes healing and reduces acid secretion

  • High-risk NSAID users → consider gastroprotection

Exam Pearl:
Treatment of NSAID-induced peptic ulcer = PPI; prevention = Misoprostol.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩) Which malignancy is commonest in AIDS patient?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Kaposi’s sarcoma is the classic and most common AIDS-associated malignancy in traditional exam settings. It is caused by infection with human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) and occurs due to severe immunosuppression in HIV infection. It commonly presents with violaceous skin lesions, but may also involve lymph nodes, gastrointestinal tract, and lungs. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is also strongly associated with AIDS and is an important AIDS-related malignancy, especially in the era of antiretroviral therapy. However, among the given options and for standard medical examinations, Kaposi’s sarcoma is the expected answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Kaposi’s sarcoma → HHV-8 associated

  • Classic AIDS-defining malignancy

  • Presents with violaceous skin lesions

  • AIDS-associated lymphoma → commonly non-Hodgkin lymphoma

  • Risk increases with severe immunosuppression (low CD4 count)

Exam Pearl:
AIDS + violaceous skin lesions = Kaposi’s sarcoma.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪) Koebner’s phenomenon is found in all except….?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Koebner’s phenomenon refers to the development of typical lesions of a skin disease at sites of trauma or injury on previously normal skin. It is classically seen in psoriasis, lichen planus, and viral warts. In psoriasis, minor trauma such as scratching can produce new psoriatic plaques. Lichen planus may also appear at sites of injury, and warts can develop following trauma due to viral inoculation. Pemphigus is not a classical disease associated with Koebner’s phenomenon, although mechanical trauma may worsen existing lesions. Therefore, among the given options, pemphigus is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Koebner phenomenon → lesions at sites of trauma

  • Classic diseases:

    • Psoriasis

    • Lichen planus

    • Vitiligo

    • Viral warts

  • Not classically associated → Pemphigus

Exam Pearl:
Koebner phenomenon = psoriasis, lichen planus, and warts; pemphigus is the exception.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫) Which is absolute contraindication of liver biopsy?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Hemangioma of the liver is an absolute contraindication to percutaneous liver biopsy because it is a highly vascular lesion and biopsy may cause severe, potentially life-threatening hemorrhage. Imaging characteristics are usually sufficient for diagnosis, and tissue sampling is avoided. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an absolute contraindication; biopsy may be performed when the diagnosis is uncertain and imaging is inconclusive. Liver cirrhosis is not an absolute contraindication, although coagulation status and bleeding risk must be assessed. Fibroma of the liver is rare and not considered a classic contraindication. Therefore, hemangioma is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Liver hemangioma → avoid biopsy due to bleeding risk

  • Liver biopsy contraindications:

    • Uncorrectable coagulopathy

    • Severe thrombocytopenia

    • Vascular liver lesions (e.g., hemangioma)

  • Cirrhosis → biopsy may be done when indicated

  • HCC → biopsy depends on diagnostic context

Exam Pearl:
Never biopsy a suspected liver hemangioma because of the risk of catastrophic bleeding.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬) A child having diarrhoea later complicated by skin rash & petechiae. What will be most likely diagnosis?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Shigella infection can cause diarrhoea followed by systemic complications, including skin manifestations such as petechiae and rash, particularly in severe infections. Shigella produces Shiga toxin, which can cause endothelial injury and may lead to complications such as hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), characterized by hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and renal impairment. The presence of petechiae suggests a possible platelet-related complication. Campylobacter is more classically associated with Guillain–Barré syndrome and reactive arthritis. Rotavirus usually causes uncomplicated watery diarrhoea in children. Yersinia may cause mesenteric lymphadenitis and reactive phenomena but is less typical for this presentation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Shigella → bloody diarrhoea + Shiga toxin

  • Complication → HUS

  • HUS triad → hemolytic anemia + thrombocytopenia + acute kidney injury

  • Campylobacter → Guillain–Barré syndrome

  • Rotavirus → common cause of childhood watery diarrhoea

Exam Pearl:
Child with diarrhoea followed by petechiae/thrombocytopenic features → think Shigella (Shiga toxin).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭) Fever that persists for several hours and always touches the baseline between attacks is called........?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Intermittent fever is characterized by fever that returns to normal baseline temperature between febrile episodes. The temperature rises for several hours and then falls back to normal, with recurrent attacks occurring at intervals. This pattern is classically seen in infections such as malaria. In remittent fever, the temperature also fluctuates but does not return to normal baseline between attacks. Continued fever remains elevated with minimal daily variation, while scarlet fever is a specific febrile illness caused by toxin-producing Streptococcus pyogenes associated with a characteristic rash.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Intermittent fever → returns to normal between attacks

  • Remittent fever → fluctuation but never reaches baseline

  • Continued fever → persistent elevation with little variation

  • Malaria → classic example of intermittent fever

Exam Pearl:
Fever that touches the baseline between attacks = intermittent fever.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮) What is the cause of splinter hemorrhage?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Splinter hemorrhages are small, linear, reddish-brown streaks seen under the nails, caused by bleeding from damaged nail bed capillaries. The classic clinical association is subacute bacterial endocarditis (SBE), where circulating immune complexes and small emboli from infected cardiac valves cause vascular injury and nail bed hemorrhage. Splinter hemorrhages can also occur due to trauma and other systemic conditions, but in medical examinations, subacute bacterial endocarditis is the most important association. Iron deficiency anemia, chronic kidney disease, and arsenic poisoning may cause other nail changes but are not classic causes of splinter hemorrhage.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Splinter hemorrhage → Subacute bacterial endocarditis

  • Appears as linear streaks under nails

  • Other endocarditis signs:

    • Janeway lesions

    • Osler nodes

    • Roth spots

  • Can also occur due to local trauma

Exam Pearl:
Splinter hemorrhage is a classic peripheral sign of infective endocarditis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯) How is the murmur of PDA?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The murmur of Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA) is classically a continuous machinery murmur heard throughout systole and diastole, best appreciated at the left upper sternal border or below the left clavicle. It occurs because blood flows continuously from the high-pressure aorta into the lower-pressure pulmonary artery during both phases of the cardiac cycle. A purely systolic murmur is common in many valvular lesions, while a pansystolic murmur is typical of conditions such as ventricular septal defect (VSD), mitral regurgitation, and tricuspid regurgitation. Therefore, the characteristic murmur of PDA is continuous.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PDA → continuous machinery murmur

  • Site → left upper sternal border

  • Due to → continuous flow from aorta to pulmonary artery

  • VSD → pansystolic murmur

  • Aortic regurgitation → early diastolic murmur

Exam Pearl:
PDA = continuous machinery murmur.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১০) Signs of impaired myocardial function excludes.....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Signs of impaired myocardial function indicate reduced cardiac output and poor tissue perfusion. Common features include oliguria due to reduced renal perfusion, cold peripheries due to peripheral vasoconstriction, and narrow pulse pressure due to reduced stroke volume, as seen in heart failure or cardiogenic shock. Hypertension is not a sign of impaired myocardial function; instead, it is a risk factor that can contribute to myocardial dysfunction by increasing afterload and cardiac workload. Therefore, among the given options, hypertension is the exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Impaired myocardial function → low cardiac output state

  • Signs:

    • Cold peripheries

    • Oliguria

    • Narrow pulse pressure

    • Hypotension

  • Narrow pulse pressure → reduced stroke volume

  • Hypertension → risk factor, not a typical sign of myocardial failure

Exam Pearl:
Heart failure signs reflect poor perfusion: cold extremities + oliguria + narrow pulse pressure.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১১) Which form of anemia is common in strict vegetarians?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Strict vegetarians are at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency, because vitamin B12 is mainly found in animal-derived foods such as meat, eggs, and dairy products. Deficiency of vitamin B12 causes impaired DNA synthesis, leading to abnormal maturation of erythrocytes and resulting in megaloblastic anemia. It is characterized by macrocytic red blood cells, hypersegmented neutrophils, and may be associated with neurological manifestations. Folate deficiency can also cause megaloblastic anemia, but in strict vegetarians, B12 deficiency is the classic association. Microcytic anemia is usually due to iron deficiency, while hemolytic and normocytic anemias are not typical.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Strict vegetarian diet → Vitamin B12 deficiency

  • Vitamin B12 deficiency → Megaloblastic anemia

  • Peripheral smear → macro-ovalocytes + hypersegmented neutrophils

  • B12 deficiency → neurological symptoms may occur

  • Iron deficiency → microcytic hypochromic anemia

Exam Pearl:
Strict vegetarian + anemia = think vitamin B12 deficiency causing megaloblastic anemia.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১২) Fallot’s pentalogy is tetralogy plus….?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Fallot’s pentalogy consists of the four features of Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) plus an additional atrial septal defect (ASD). The four components of TOF are: ventricular septal defect (VSD), pulmonary stenosis, overriding of the aorta, and right ventricular hypertrophy (RVH). When ASD is also present, the condition is called Fallot’s pentalogy. PDA is not the additional component of Fallot’s pentalogy. AS (aortic stenosis) and LVH are not associated features. Therefore, ASD is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tetralogy of Fallot = VSD + pulmonary stenosis + overriding aorta + RVH

  • Fallot’s pentalogy = TOF + ASD

  • Most common cyanotic congenital heart disease → TOF

  • Boot-shaped heart on X-ray → TOF

Exam Pearl:
Pentalogy of Fallot = Tetralogy of Fallot + ASD.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১৩) Where step ladder pattern of fever occurs?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The step-ladder pattern of fever is classically associated with enteric (typhoid) fever caused by Salmonella Typhi. In this pattern, the body temperature rises gradually in a stepwise manner over several days, reaching a sustained high level. This occurs due to progressive bacterial multiplication and systemic inflammatory response. Malaria typically produces intermittent or periodic fever with chills and rigors. Septicemia usually causes high-grade fever with variable patterns, and kala-azar is associated with prolonged irregular fever rather than a step-ladder pattern.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Step-ladder fever → Enteric (typhoid) fever

  • Typhoid organism → Salmonella Typhi

  • Malaria → intermittent fever

  • Kala-azar → prolonged fever with hepatosplenomegaly

  • Septicemia → continuous/irregular high fever

Exam Pearl:
Step-ladder rise of temperature = Typhoid fever.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১৪) What is the cause of non-pitting edema?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Myxedema is a classic cause of non-pitting edema. In hypothyroidism, accumulation of glycosaminoglycans (mucopolysaccharides) in the interstitial tissues increases water retention and produces a firm, doughy swelling that does not pit on pressure. In contrast, edema due to heart failure (HF), nephrotic syndrome (NS), and liver cirrhosis is typically pitting edema caused by fluid accumulation in the interstitial space. Therefore, among the given options, myxedema is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Non-pitting edema → Myxedema

  • Cause → accumulation of glycosaminoglycans

  • Hypothyroidism features:

    • Cold intolerance

    • Weight gain

    • Bradycardia

    • Dry skin

  • HF, NS, cirrhosis → usually pitting edema

Exam Pearl:
Non-pitting edema is a hallmark of myxedema (hypothyroidism).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১৫) What is the cause of differential clubbing?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Differential clubbing occurs classically in Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA) with pulmonary hypertension and right-to-left shunting (Eisenmenger syndrome). In PDA, deoxygenated blood enters the descending aorta through the ductus, causing cyanosis and clubbing in the lower limbs, while the upper limbs remain relatively spared because branches to the upper body arise before the ductus. This produces differential cyanosis and differential clubbing. TOF causes generalized cyanosis and clubbing, while VSD and ASD do not typically produce differential clubbing.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Differential clubbing → PDA with Eisenmenger syndrome

  • Upper limbs → relatively normal

  • Lower limbs → cyanotic and clubbed

  • Mechanism → right-to-left shunt through PDA into descending aorta

  • TOF → generalized clubbing

Exam Pearl:
Differential clubbing = PDA with pulmonary hypertension (Eisenmenger PDA).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১৬) What is the cause of rusty sputum?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Rusty sputum is a classic clinical feature of pneumococcal pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. It occurs due to the presence of red blood cells mixed with inflammatory exudate in the sputum, giving it a rusty or brownish appearance. Pneumococcal pneumonia commonly presents with sudden onset fever, pleuritic chest pain, productive cough, and lobar consolidation. Pulmonary tuberculosis may cause blood-streaked sputum or hemoptysis, bronchiectasis can cause large amounts of purulent sputum, and lung abscess typically produces foul-smelling purulent sputum.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Rusty sputum → Pneumococcal pneumonia

  • Organism → Streptococcus pneumoniae

  • Classic presentation → lobar pneumonia

  • Bronchiectasis → copious purulent sputum

  • Lung abscess → foul-smelling sputum

Exam Pearl:
Rusty sputum is a hallmark of pneumococcal lobar pneumon

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১৭) Delta wave in ECG is found in….?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
A delta wave is the characteristic ECG finding of Wolff–Parkinson–White (WPW) syndrome. It occurs due to the presence of an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that allows electrical impulses to bypass the normal AV node conduction pathway and activate the ventricles prematurely. This causes a slurred initial upstroke of the QRS complex, known as the delta wave, along with a shortened PR interval and widened QRS complex. Sick sinus syndrome, hypothermia, and hypernatremia do not produce delta waves.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • WPW syndrome → Delta wave

  • Cause → Accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent)

  • ECG features:

    • Short PR interval

    • Delta wave

    • Wide QRS complex

  • WPW predisposes to supraventricular tachycardia (AVRT)

Exam Pearl:
Delta wave + short PR interval = Wolff–Parkinson–White syndrome.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১৮) What is the possible finding in hand examination of a patient with bronchiectasis?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Clubbing is a classic peripheral sign found in patients with bronchiectasis due to chronic suppurative lung disease and persistent hypoxia. Recurrent infection and chronic inflammation in bronchiectasis can stimulate vascular and connective tissue changes in the nail bed, leading to bulbous enlargement of the fingertips and loss of the nail bed angle. Cyanosis may occur in severe cases but is not the characteristic hand finding. Anemia and leukonychia are not typical features of bronchiectasis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bronchiectasis → Clubbing

  • Other causes of clubbing:

    • Lung carcinoma

    • Cystic fibrosis

    • Lung abscess

    • Cyanotic congenital heart disease

    • Infective endocarditis

  • Bronchiectasis features:

    • Chronic productive cough

    • Recurrent chest infections

    • Hemoptysis

Exam Pearl:
Chronic suppurative lung disease + finger clubbing = bronchiectasis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১৯) Vertigo in older patients is most commonly due to....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The most common cause of vertigo in older patients is Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). It occurs due to displacement of otoconia (calcium carbonate crystals) from the utricle into the semicircular canals, causing brief episodes of vertigo triggered by head movements such as turning in bed or looking upward. Cerebellopontine angle lesions (e.g., vestibular schwannoma) are less common and usually present with hearing loss or neurological signs. Dementia does not cause true vertigo, and vestibular neuritis can cause acute prolonged vertigo but is not the commonest cause in elderly patients.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • BPPV → most common cause of vertigo in elderly

  • Trigger → change in head position

  • Cause → displaced otoconia in semicircular canal

  • Vestibular neuritis → acute continuous vertigo, usually post-viral

  • Cerebellopontine angle tumor → vertigo + hearing loss

Exam Pearl:
Elderly patient with positional vertigo = BPPV (most common cause).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২০) Which is the most common factor predisposing aortic dissection?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The most common predisposing factor for aortic dissection is hypertension. Chronic high blood pressure causes increased stress on the aortic wall, leading to degeneration of the media layer and making it susceptible to a tear. The tear allows blood to enter the aortic wall, creating a false lumen. Other risk factors include connective tissue disorders such as Marfan syndrome, bicuspid aortic valve, and pre-existing aortic aneurysm. Atherosclerosis is associated with many vascular diseases but is not the primary risk factor for aortic dissection. “Aortic contraction” is not a recognized risk factor.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common risk factor of aortic dissection → Hypertension

  • Site of tear → usually ascending aorta or descending thoracic aorta

  • Classic symptom → sudden severe tearing chest pain

  • Risk factors:

    • Marfan syndrome

    • Bicuspid aortic valve

    • Aortic aneurysm

Exam Pearl:
Aortic dissection in an adult patient = think hypertension first.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২১) What is the earliest change in ECG in AMI?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The earliest ECG change in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is T-wave change, typically hyperacute T waves (tall, broad-based T waves), which may later progress to T-wave inversion due to myocardial ischemia. Among the given options, T-inversion is the earliest recognized ischemic ECG change. ST elevation occurs later and indicates acute transmural myocardial injury. Pathological Q waves develop later due to myocardial necrosis and indicate established infarction. Absent P waves are not a feature of AMI. Therefore, T-wave inversion is the best answer among the given choices.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ECG progression in AMI:

    1. Hyperacute T wave

    2. ST elevation

    3. T-wave inversion

    4. Pathological Q wave

  • ST elevation → acute myocardial injury

  • Pathological Q wave → myocardial necrosis

  • T-wave inversion → ischemia

Exam Pearl:
Earliest ECG manifestation of AMI is T-wave change (hyperacute T wave/T inversion).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২২) Which one is a major criteria for rheumatic fever?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
According to the Jones criteria, subcutaneous nodules are one of the major criteria for the diagnosis of rheumatic fever. The major criteria include migratory polyarthritis, carditis, Sydenham chorea, erythema marginatum, and subcutaneous nodules. Arthralgia and fever are minor criteria, while raised ESR is also a minor criterion indicating inflammation. Subcutaneous nodules are painless, firm, small nodules usually found over bony prominences or extensor surfaces and are associated with more severe rheumatic carditis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Major Jones criteria:

    • Migratory polyarthritis

    • Carditis

    • Sydenham chorea

    • Erythema marginatum

    • Subcutaneous nodules

  • Minor criteria:

    • Fever

    • Arthralgia

    • Raised ESR/CRP

    • Prolonged PR interval

Exam Pearl:
Subcutaneous nodules = major Jones criterion for rheumatic fever.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২৩) Deficiency of which vitamin may causes high output cardiac failure?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency can cause high-output cardiac failure due to beriberi heart disease. Thiamine is essential for carbohydrate metabolism, and its deficiency leads to impaired energy production, peripheral vasodilation, increased venous return, and increased cardiac workload. This results in a high-output state that may progress to heart failure. Niacin deficiency causes pellagra, pyridoxine deficiency causes neuropathy and sideroblastic anemia, and biotin deficiency is rare and mainly associated with dermatitis and neurological symptoms.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thiamine deficiency → Wet beriberi → high-output heart failure

  • Dry beriberi → peripheral neuropathy

  • Thiamine deficiency risk:

    • Chronic alcoholism

    • Malnutrition

    • Prolonged vomiting

  • Niacin deficiency → Pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia)

Exam Pearl:
High-output cardiac failure + vitamin deficiency = Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২৪) Which is a cause of monoarthritis?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Gout is a classic cause of acute monoarthritis, most commonly affecting the first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra). It occurs due to deposition of monosodium urate crystals in the joint, causing intense inflammation and pain. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), SLE, and ankylosing spondylitis are typically associated with oligoarthritis or polyarthritis patterns rather than isolated monoarthritis. Although other conditions can occasionally present as monoarthritis, gout is the most common and characteristic answer among the given options.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gout → acute monoarthritis

  • Most common joint → 1st MTP joint (podagra)

  • Crystal → monosodium urate

  • Synovial fluid → needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals

  • Septic arthritis → important differential diagnosis of acute monoarthritis

Exam Pearl:
Painful red swollen single joint = think gout (monoarthritis).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২৫) Which drug is commonly used in AF patient with bronchial asthma?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
In a patient with atrial fibrillation (AF) and bronchial asthma, diltiazem is commonly preferred for ventricular rate control because it is a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that slows conduction through the AV node without causing bronchoconstriction. Beta blockers are generally avoided or used cautiously in asthma because they may precipitate bronchospasm by blocking β₂ receptors. Digoxin can be used in selected cases, especially with heart failure or sedentary patients, but it is less effective for rate control during exertion. Amiodarone may be used for rhythm control in certain situations but is not the usual first choice for rate control.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • AF rate control drugs:

    • Beta blockers

    • Non-DHP calcium channel blockers (Diltiazem, Verapamil)

    • Digoxin

  • Asthma + AF → avoid non-selective beta blockers

  • Diltiazem → AV nodal blockade, no bronchospasm

  • Amiodarone → rhythm control drug

Exam Pearl:
AF with bronchial asthma → choose diltiazem instead of beta blockers.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২৬) When HTN is not controlled with combination of 3 drugs is called..?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Resistant hypertension is defined as blood pressure that remains above the target despite the use of three antihypertensive drugs of different classes, usually including a diuretic, at optimal doses. It may also refer to blood pressure that requires four or more medications to achieve control. Refractory hypertension is a more severe and uncommon form where BP remains uncontrolled despite multiple medications, typically including a diuretic and several other agents. Malignant hypertension refers to severe hypertension with acute target-organ damage, while hypertensive encephalopathy involves neurological symptoms due to severe hypertension.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Resistant HTN → uncontrolled BP despite 3 drugs including a diuretic

  • Common causes:

    • Poor adherence

    • Secondary hypertension

    • Inadequate drug regimen

  • Malignant HTN → severe BP + acute organ damage

  • Refractory HTN → extreme resistant form

Exam Pearl:
BP uncontrolled despite 3 antihypertensive drugs = Resistant hypertension.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২৭) What is the nature of pain in PUD?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The typical pain of peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is described as burning or gnawing epigastric pain. It is related to acid exposure and mucosal ulceration in the stomach or duodenum. In duodenal ulcer, pain often occurs when the stomach is empty and may be relieved by food, while in gastric ulcer, pain may worsen after meals. Choking, throbbing, and colicky pains are not characteristic descriptions of PUD pain.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PUD pain → burning/gnawing epigastric pain

  • Duodenal ulcer:

    • Pain relieved by food

    • Night pain common

  • Gastric ulcer:

    • Pain aggravated by meals

  • Complications:

    • Bleeding

    • Perforation

    • Gastric outlet obstruction

Exam Pearl:
Peptic ulcer pain is classically burning epigastric pain.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২৮) Honeycomb appearance in X-ray is found in....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
A honeycomb appearance on chest X-ray/HRCT is classically seen in pulmonary fibrosis, especially idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). It represents end-stage fibrotic lung disease with destruction of normal lung architecture and formation of multiple small cystic air spaces due to bronchiolar dilation and fibrosis. Bronchiectasis can show tram-track and signet-ring appearances, while bronchial carcinoma may show a mass lesion. Lung abscess typically appears as a cavity with an air-fluid level. Therefore, pulmonary fibrosis is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Honeycomb lung → Pulmonary fibrosis (especially IPF)

  • HRCT features of IPF:

    • Subpleural fibrosis

    • Reticular shadows

    • Honeycombing

  • Bronchiectasis → tram-track sign, signet-ring sign

  • Lung abscess → cavity with air-fluid level

Exam Pearl:
Honeycomb appearance = end-stage pulmonary fibrosis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ২৯) Prader-willi syndrome is characterized by all except….?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Prader–Willi syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by loss of expression of paternal chromosome 15q11–q13. It is characterized by neonatal hypotonia, developmental delay/intellectual disability, hyperphagia leading to obesity, and hypogonadism due to hypothalamic dysfunction. Hypertonia is not a feature; instead, affected infants classically present with marked hypotonia and poor feeding initially. Therefore, among the given options, hypertonia is the exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Prader–Willi syndrome:

    • Paternal chromosome 15 deletion

    • Hypotonia

    • Hyperphagia → obesity

    • Hypogonadism

    • Intellectual disability

  • Angelman syndrome → maternal chromosome 15 deletion

Exam Pearl:
Prader–Willi = hypotonia + hyperphagia + obesity + hypogonadism.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩০) Which pulmonary vascular disease is indication for lung transplantation?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Eisenmenger’s syndrome is a severe form of pulmonary vascular disease caused by long-standing left-to-right shunts (e.g., VSD, ASD, PDA) leading to irreversible pulmonary vascular remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, and reversal of shunt direction. In advanced cases, heart-lung transplantation or lung transplantation with repair of the cardiac defect may be indicated. Cystic fibrosis, pulmonary fibrosis, and lymphangioleiomyomatosis are important indications for lung transplantation but are primarily parenchymal lung diseases, not pulmonary vascular diseases. Therefore, Eisenmenger’s syndrome is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Eisenmenger syndrome → pulmonary vascular disease

  • Due to → irreversible pulmonary hypertension from congenital shunts

  • Advanced cases → lung/heart-lung transplantation

  • Common pulmonary vascular transplant indication → severe pulmonary arterial hypertension

Exam Pearl:
Pulmonary vascular disease requiring transplantation = Eisenmenger syndrome.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩১) What type of jaundice occurs in malaria?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Jaundice in malaria can occur due to multiple mechanisms, so it may have hemolytic, hepatocellular, and obstructive components. Hemolytic jaundice is common due to destruction of parasitized and non-parasitized red blood cells, causing increased bilirubin production. Hepatocellular dysfunction may occur due to hepatic involvement, especially in severe malaria. Obstructive features may occur due to impaired bile flow (cholestasis), particularly in severe infections. Therefore, among the given options, all of them is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Malaria jaundice → may be mixed type

  • Main mechanism → hemolysis of RBCs

  • Severe malaria → hepatic dysfunction + cholestasis may occur

  • Plasmodium falciparum → commonly associated with severe complications

Exam Pearl:
Malaria-associated jaundice is usually mixed: hemolytic + hepatocellular ± obstructive.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩২) Which is the absolute indication of steroids along with anti-TB drugs?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Tubercular meningitis (TBM) is an absolute indication for adjunctive corticosteroid therapy along with standard anti-tubercular drugs. Steroids reduce inflammation, cerebral edema, and the risk of complications such as raised intracranial pressure, neurological deficits, and mortality. In TB pericarditis and other extrapulmonary TB forms, steroids may be considered in selected situations, but they are not universally mandatory. Bilateral adrenal TB requires anti-TB therapy and management of adrenal insufficiency but is not an indication for routine steroid addition for the infection itself.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • TB meningitis → steroids indicated

  • Benefit of steroids:

    • Reduce inflammation

    • Decrease cerebral edema

    • Improve survival

  • Other conditions where steroids may be used selectively:

    • TB pericarditis

    • Severe inflammatory complications

Exam Pearl:
All patients with tubercular meningitis should receive corticosteroids with anti-TB therapy.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩৩) Which of the following case is to be treated under category-1 anti-TB treatment regimen?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Category-1 anti-TB treatment regimen is used for new TB cases, including new smear-positive pulmonary TB, new smear-negative pulmonary TB with extensive disease, and severe extra-pulmonary TB (such as tubercular meningitis or disseminated TB). Relapse, treatment failure, and treatment after default are considered previously treated cases and were traditionally managed under Category-2 regimen with additional drugs. Therefore, among the given options, severe extra-pulmonary TB is the correct indication for Category-1 treatment.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Category-1 TB regimen → New TB cases

  • Includes:

    • New smear-positive pulmonary TB

    • Severe extra-pulmonary TB

    • Extensive new smear-negative pulmonary TB

  • Category-2 → Previously treated cases:

    • Relapse

    • Failure

    • Treatment after default

Exam Pearl:
Severe extra-pulmonary TB in a new patient = Category-1 anti-TB regimen.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩৪) Which investigation is more sensitive to diagnose bronchiectasis?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest is the most sensitive and preferred investigation for diagnosing bronchiectasis. HRCT demonstrates characteristic structural changes such as bronchial dilatation, lack of normal bronchial tapering, and the signet-ring sign. Chest X-ray may show indirect findings like tram-track opacities and is less sensitive, especially in early disease. MRI and PET are not routine diagnostic investigations for bronchiectasis. Therefore, HRCT is the investigation of choice.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bronchiectasis diagnosis → HRCT chest

  • HRCT findings:

    • Bronchial dilatation

    • Lack of tapering

    • Signet-ring sign

    • Tram-track appearance

  • CXR → less sensitive, may be normal in mild disease

Exam Pearl:
Best and most sensitive test for bronchiectasis = HRCT chest.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩৫) Which is the cause of unilateral pleural effusion?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Unilateral pleural effusion is commonly caused by local pleural or adjacent organ pathology, and pancreatitis can produce a unilateral pleural effusion, usually on the left side, due to diaphragmatic irritation or pancreaticopleural fistula. In contrast, systemic causes such as congestive cardiac failure (CCF), nephrotic syndrome (NS), and chronic liver disease (CLD) typically produce bilateral pleural effusions due to generalized fluid imbalance (increased hydrostatic pressure or reduced oncotic pressure). Therefore, pancreatitis is the best answer among the given options.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pancreatitis → left-sided pleural effusion

  • CCF → usually bilateral transudative effusion

  • NS → bilateral effusion due to hypoalbuminemia

  • CLD/cirrhosis → bilateral effusion (hepatic hydrothorax, usually right-sided)

Exam Pearl:
Unilateral pleural effusion with abdominal pathology = think pancreatitis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩৬) Which feature is true about thyrotoxicosis?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Weight loss is a classic feature of thyrotoxicosis due to increased basal metabolic rate and enhanced catabolism of fat and protein, even when appetite is increased. Excess thyroid hormone increases sympathetic activity and metabolic processes, causing symptoms such as heat intolerance, sweating, palpitations, tremor, and anxiety. Constipation, husky voice, and increased sleep are more typical of hypothyroidism due to reduced metabolic activity and mucopolysaccharide deposition. Therefore, weight loss is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thyrotoxicosis features:

    • Weight loss

    • Heat intolerance

    • Palpitations

    • Tremor

    • Increased sweating

    • Hyperactivity

  • Hypothyroidism:

    • Weight gain

    • Constipation

    • Hoarse/husky voice

    • Excessive sleepiness

Exam Pearl:
Thyrotoxicosis burns energy → weight loss despite increased appetite.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩৭) What is the specific investigation for legionella pneumonia?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The specific investigation for Legionella pneumonia is detection of Legionella urinary antigen. It is a rapid and specific test, mainly detecting Legionella pneumophila serogroup 1, which is responsible for most cases of community-acquired Legionella pneumonia. CXR and HRCT can show pneumonia but are not specific. Sputum studies may be used for culture or PCR, but they are less commonly used for rapid diagnosis. Legionella pneumonia often presents with high fever, dry cough, gastrointestinal symptoms, and hyponatremia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Legionella pneumonia → urinary antigen test

  • Common organism → Legionella pneumophila

  • Associated features:

    • High fever

    • Relative bradycardia

    • Hyponatremia

    • GI symptoms

  • Culture requires special media (BCYE agar)

Exam Pearl:
Specific rapid test for Legionella pneumonia = urinary antigen detection.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩৮) Daily steroid tablet is recommended for which step of management of asthma control?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
In the stepwise management of asthma, daily oral corticosteroids are reserved for Step 5, which represents severe persistent asthma not controlled despite maximal inhaled therapy. At this stage, patients may require regular low-dose oral steroids in addition to high-dose inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting bronchodilator therapy and consideration of biologic therapies. Earlier steps (Step 2–4) mainly involve inhaled corticosteroids with increasing intensity and add-on medications such as LABA or other controllers. Long-term oral steroid use is avoided whenever possible due to significant adverse effects.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Step 5 asthma → daily oral corticosteroid may be required

  • Stepwise escalation:

    • Step 1 → reliever as needed

    • Step 2 → low-dose ICS

    • Step 3 → low-dose ICS + LABA

    • Step 4 → medium/high-dose ICS + LABA

    • Step 5 → add oral steroid/biologic therapy

  • Long-term steroids → risk of osteoporosis, diabetes, adrenal suppression

Exam Pearl:
Regular daily oral steroid = Step 5 severe asthma management.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৩৯) Which anti TB drug may be responsible for development of gout?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Pyrazinamide can cause hyperuricemia and gout as an adverse effect. It reduces renal excretion of uric acid, leading to increased serum urate levels and possible precipitation of monosodium urate crystals in joints, causing gouty arthritis. Ethambutol may also rarely increase uric acid levels, but pyrazinamide is the classic and most commonly tested anti-TB drug associated with gout. Isoniazid and rifampicin are not typical causes of hyperuricemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pyrazinamide → hyperuricemia → gout

  • Ethambutol → optic neuritis

  • Isoniazid → peripheral neuropathy, hepatitis

  • Rifampicin → orange discoloration of body fluids, hepatotoxicity

Exam Pearl:
Anti-TB drug causing gout = Pyrazinamide.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪০) All of the following drugs are used to treat prolactinoma except.....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Brinzolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used mainly in the treatment of glaucoma by reducing aqueous humor production; it has no role in treating prolactinoma. Prolactinomas are usually treated with dopamine agonists, which suppress prolactin secretion and reduce tumor size. Bromocriptine, cabergoline, and quinagolide are dopamine agonists used in the management of hyperprolactinemia due to prolactinoma. Among these, cabergoline is often preferred due to better efficacy and tolerability.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Prolactinoma treatment → Dopamine agonists

  • Drugs:

    • Cabergoline

    • Bromocriptine

    • Quinagolide

  • Dopamine agonists → ↓ prolactin secretion + tumor shrinkage

  • Brinzolamide → glaucoma treatment

Exam Pearl:
Prolactinoma is treated with dopamine agonists, not brinzolamide.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪১) What should be duration of antibiotic coverage in lung abscess?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The usual duration of antibiotic therapy for lung abscess is 6–10 weeks, depending on clinical and radiological response. Lung abscess is a localized collection of pus within the lung, commonly caused by anaerobic bacteria following aspiration. Prolonged antibiotic therapy is required because penetration into the abscess cavity is slow and resolution occurs gradually. Treatment is continued until there is significant clinical improvement and radiological resolution. Shorter courses such as 2–4 weeks are generally insufficient for uncomplicated lung abscess management.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Lung abscess → antibiotics for 6–10 weeks

  • Common cause → aspiration of anaerobic organisms

  • Clinical features:

    • Fever

    • Productive cough

    • Foul-smelling sputum

  • Imaging → cavity with air-fluid level

Exam Pearl:
Lung abscess requires prolonged antibiotics: approximately 6–10 weeks.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪২) KF rings are found in....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Kayser–Fleischer (KF) rings are a characteristic finding of Wilson’s disease. They are caused by deposition of copper in Descemet’s membrane of the cornea, producing a greenish-brown ring at the corneal periphery. Wilson’s disease occurs due to defective copper metabolism caused by ATP7B gene mutation, leading to copper accumulation in the liver, brain, and eyes. Hemochromatosis involves iron overload, Gilbert’s syndrome causes unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and Budd–Chiari syndrome is due to hepatic venous outflow obstruction.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • KF ring → Wilson’s disease

  • Cause → copper deposition in cornea

  • Gene → ATP7B mutation

  • Associated features:

    • Liver disease

    • Neuropsychiatric symptoms

    • Low ceruloplasmin level

  • Hemochromatosis → iron deposition

Exam Pearl:
Kayser–Fleischer ring = copper accumulation = Wilson’s disease.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪৩) Discoloration of the area around umbilicus due to hemorrhagic ascites in acute pancreatitis is called..... ?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Cullen's sign refers to bluish discoloration around the umbilicus due to intra-abdominal hemorrhage, classically seen in hemorrhagic acute pancreatitis. It occurs when blood tracks through the fascial planes to the periumbilical region. Grey Turner's sign is flank discoloration due to retroperitoneal bleeding and may also occur in severe pancreatitis. Murphy's sign indicates acute cholecystitis, and Hutchinson's sign is associated with other conditions (e.g., herpes zoster/ocular involvement or melanoma depending on context), not hemorrhagic pancreatitis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cullen's sign → periumbilical ecchymosis

  • Cause → intra-abdominal bleeding

  • Classic association → hemorrhagic acute pancreatitis

  • Grey Turner's sign → flank ecchymosis

  • Both Cullen and Grey Turner signs indicate severe hemorrhagic pancreatitis

Exam Pearl:
Periumbilical bruising in acute pancreatitis = Cullen's sign.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪৪) Hurthle cells are pathognomonic of…..?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Hurthle cells (also called oncocytic cells) are classically associated with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. They are transformed thyroid follicular cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm due to increased mitochondrial content, occurring as a result of chronic autoimmune thyroid destruction. Although Hurthle cells can also be seen in other thyroid conditions and tumors, their classic exam association is Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. Graves’ disease is characterized by diffuse thyroid hyperplasia, scalloped colloid, and lymphocytic infiltration, but not Hurthle cell change as a typical finding.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hurthle cells → Hashimoto’s thyroiditis

  • Hashimoto’s features:

    • Autoimmune thyroid destruction

    • Anti-TPO antibodies

    • Lymphoid follicles

    • Hurthle cell change

  • Graves’ disease:

    • Diffuse goiter

    • Ophthalmopathy

    • Pretibial myxedema

Exam Pearl:
Hurthle cell change is a classic histological feature of Hashimoto’s thyroiditis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪৫) Which is the most common cause of Cushing’s syndrome?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The most common cause of Cushing’s syndrome overall is iatrogenic corticosteroid use (exogenous glucocorticoid therapy). Prolonged administration of drugs such as prednisolone can produce features of cortisol excess, including central obesity, hypertension, diabetes, osteoporosis, and skin changes. Among endogenous causes, the most common is Cushing’s disease, which is due to a pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma. Adrenal tumors are less common causes. Therefore, for the question asking the most common cause of Cushing’s syndrome, iatrogenic steroid use is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common cause of Cushing’s syndrome → Iatrogenic

  • Most common endogenous cause → Cushing’s disease

  • Cushing’s disease → pituitary ACTH adenoma

  • Features:

    • Central obesity

    • Moon face

    • Hypertension

    • Purple striae

    • Hyperglycemia

Exam Pearl:
Cushing’s syndrome overall = exogenous steroids; endogenous = pituitary Cushing’s disease.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪৬) Which is the gold standard but invasive & seldom used test of pancreatic function?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.option4: Collection of pure pancreatic juice after secretin injection
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The secretin stimulation test with collection of pure pancreatic juice is considered the gold standard test for pancreatic exocrine function, although it is invasive and rarely used in clinical practice. Secretin stimulates pancreatic ductal cells to release bicarbonate-rich fluid, which is collected and analyzed for pancreatic function assessment. USG is useful for structural evaluation but not functional assessment. MRCP and ERCP are imaging techniques for pancreaticobiliary ducts; ERCP is invasive but mainly diagnostic/therapeutic for ductal pathology, not the gold standard for pancreatic function.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gold standard pancreatic function test → Secretin stimulation test

  • Measures:

    • Bicarbonate secretion

    • Pancreatic enzyme output

  • Non-invasive alternatives:

    • Fecal elastase test

    • 13C breath tests

  • ERCP → mainly therapeutic (stones, strictures, stenting)

Exam Pearl:
Secretin-stimulated pure pancreatic juice collection = gold standard for exocrine pancreatic function.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪৭) Which is a cause of tender hepatomegaly?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Budd–Chiari syndrome is a classic cause of tender hepatomegaly due to obstruction of hepatic venous outflow, causing hepatic congestion, stretching of the liver capsule, and abdominal pain. The liver becomes enlarged and tender, often associated with ascites and abnormal liver function tests. Malaria, kala-azar, and lymphoma can cause hepatomegaly, but the liver is usually non-tender due to gradual enlargement. Tender hepatomegaly typically suggests acute inflammation or congestion of the liver.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tender hepatomegaly causes:

    • Budd–Chiari syndrome

    • Acute hepatitis

    • Liver congestion (heart failure)

    • Liver abscess

  • Budd–Chiari syndrome:

    • Hepatic vein obstruction

    • Hepatomegaly + abdominal pain + ascites

Exam Pearl:
Painful/tender enlarged liver = think hepatic congestion, especially Budd–Chiari syndrome.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪৮) Which type of tremor of the extended hand is found in acute liver failure?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The tremor seen in acute liver failure is flapping tremor (asterixis). It is a form of negative myoclonus caused by brief interruptions of sustained muscle contraction. It is commonly seen in hepatic encephalopathy due to accumulation of neurotoxic substances, especially ammonia, resulting from impaired liver detoxification. The patient is asked to extend the hands and dorsiflex the wrists; sudden downward movements (flapping) indicate asterixis. Resting tremor is typical of Parkinsonism, while intention tremor occurs with cerebellar lesions.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Asterixis (flapping tremor) → hepatic encephalopathy

  • Seen in:

    • Liver failure

    • Renal failure (uremia)

    • Respiratory failure (CO₂ retention)

  • Due to → negative myoclonus

  • Test → hands extended with wrists dorsiflexed

Exam Pearl:
Extended hand + liver failure + flapping movement = asterixis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৪৯) Which is a non-invasive test for H. Pylori detection?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The urea breath test is a non-invasive test for detecting Helicobacter pylori infection. It is based on the ability of H. pylori to produce urease enzyme, which breaks down labeled urea into ammonia and labeled carbon dioxide that can be detected in the patient's breath. Histology, rapid urease test, and microbiological culture require gastric biopsy obtained during endoscopy, making them invasive tests. The urea breath test is highly sensitive and is also commonly used to confirm eradication after treatment.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Non-invasive H. pylori tests:

    • Urea breath test

    • Stool antigen test

  • Invasive tests (endoscopic biopsy):

    • Histology

    • Rapid urease test

    • Culture

  • H. pylori enzyme → urease

  • Urea breath test → detects labeled CO₂

Exam Pearl:
Best non-invasive test for H. pylori = Urea breath test.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫০) MEN-2 excludes.....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
MEN type 2 (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2) is characterized by a combination of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism (especially MEN 2A). It is caused by mutations in the RET proto-oncogene. Pituitary tumors are not a feature of MEN-2; they are associated with MEN type 1, along with parathyroid hyperplasia and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Therefore, pituitary tumor is the correct exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • MEN-2 → RET mutation

  • MEN-2A:

    • Medullary thyroid carcinoma

    • Pheochromocytoma

    • Hyperparathyroidism

  • MEN-2B:

    • Medullary thyroid carcinoma

    • Pheochromocytoma

    • Mucosal neuromas

    • Marfanoid habitus

  • MEN-1 → Pituitary + Parathyroid + Pancreatic tumors

Exam Pearl:
Pituitary tumor belongs to MEN-1, not MEN-2.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫১) Recurrent abdominal pain in association with abnormal defecation in the absence of a structural abnormality of the gut is called........?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by recurrent abdominal pain associated with altered bowel habits (abnormal defecation) in the absence of any structural abnormality of the gut. The diagnosis is based on clinical criteria (Rome IV criteria). Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) involves structural inflammation of the intestine, while peptic ulcer disease (PUD) causes mucosal ulceration. Non-ulcer dyspepsia (NUD) presents mainly with upper gastrointestinal symptoms such as epigastric discomfort without ulceration, not typically with abnormal defecation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • IBS → abdominal pain + altered bowel habit + no structural lesion

  • Rome IV criteria:

    • Recurrent abdominal pain

    • Related to defecation

    • Change in stool frequency or form

  • IBS types:

    • IBS-D → diarrhea predominant

    • IBS-C → constipation predominant

Exam Pearl:
Functional bowel disorder with pain + abnormal defecation = IBS.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫২) Which is usually the initial symptom of CKD?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The initial symptom of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is commonly nocturia due to impaired urinary concentrating ability. Early in CKD, damaged nephrons lose the ability to concentrate urine, causing increased urine production at night and frequent nighttime urination. As renal function declines further, symptoms such as fatigue (due to anemia and uremia), nausea, vomiting, and other uremic manifestations appear. Hematuria is not a typical early symptom of CKD and is more suggestive of specific renal diseases.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Early CKD symptom → Nocturia

  • Cause → impaired renal concentrating ability

  • Late CKD features:

    • Fatigue

    • Anorexia

    • Nausea/vomiting

    • Pruritus

    • Uremia

  • CKD diagnosis → persistent kidney abnormality >3 months

Exam Pearl:
Nocturia is an early clue of CKD due to loss of concentrating ability.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫৩) Which is antidote for opioids poisoning?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Naloxone is the specific antidote for opioid poisoning. It is a competitive opioid receptor antagonist, mainly acting at the μ-opioid receptors, and rapidly reverses opioid-induced effects such as respiratory depression, CNS depression, and miosis. Pralidoxime is used for organophosphate poisoning, dimercaprol is a chelating agent used for heavy metal poisoning, and flumazenil is the antidote for benzodiazepine overdose.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Opioid overdose → Naloxone

  • Opioid toxidrome:

    • Respiratory depression

    • Coma

    • Pinpoint pupils

  • Pralidoxime → organophosphate poisoning

  • Flumazenil → benzodiazepine overdose

Exam Pearl:
Coma + respiratory depression + pinpoint pupils = give naloxone.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫৪) Which is the most common cause of oral thrush?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Oral thrush is the characteristic oral manifestation of Candida infection, most commonly caused by Candida albicans. It presents as creamy white plaques on the oral mucosa that can often be scraped off, leaving an erythematous base. It is commonly seen in conditions causing immunosuppression or altered oral flora, such as HIV infection, diabetes mellitus, malignancy, and prolonged antibiotic or steroid use. Follicular tonsillitis, tonsillitis, and diphtheria do not typically cause oral thrush.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Oral thrush → Candida albicans

  • Risk factors:

    • HIV/AIDS

    • Diabetes mellitus

    • Broad-spectrum antibiotics

    • Inhaled corticosteroids

  • Lesion:

    • White plaques

    • Scrape off leaving red mucosa

Exam Pearl:
Oral thrush = Candida infection (usually Candida albicans).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫৫) Which one is not pathophysiology of Type-2 DM?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.option4: Elevated plasma glucose & free fatty acids
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The main pathophysiological mechanisms of Type 2 diabetes mellitus are insulin resistance and progressive β-cell dysfunction/failure, leading to inadequate insulin secretion and persistent hyperglycemia. Increased plasma glucose and elevated free fatty acids (lipotoxicity) contribute to worsening insulin resistance and β-cell damage. Insulinitis (inflammatory infiltration of pancreatic islets) is a characteristic feature of Type 1 diabetes mellitus, where autoimmune destruction of β-cells occurs, and it is not a primary mechanism of Type 2 DM.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Type 2 DM pathogenesis:

    • Insulin resistance

    • Progressive β-cell failure

    • Increased hepatic glucose production

    • Glucotoxicity and lipotoxicity

  • Insulitis → Type 1 DM

  • Type 2 DM → usually associated with obesity and metabolic syndrome

Exam Pearl:
Insulitis is a Type 1 DM feature, not Type 2 DM.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫৬) Which oral anti diabetic drug is incretin mimetic?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Sitagliptin is an oral anti-diabetic drug that acts through the incretin pathway. It is a DPP-4 inhibitor, which prevents the breakdown of endogenous incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP), thereby increasing glucose-dependent insulin secretion and reducing glucagon release. Strictly speaking, DPP-4 inhibitors are incretin enhancers, while GLP-1 receptor agonists are true incretin mimetics; however, among the given oral drugs, sitagliptin is the accepted exam answer. Glimepiride stimulates insulin release, metformin decreases hepatic glucose production, and rosiglitazone improves insulin sensitivity via PPAR-γ activation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sitagliptin → DPP-4 inhibitor → ↑ GLP-1/GIP action

  • DPP-4 inhibitors:

    • Sitagliptin

    • Saxagliptin

    • Linagliptin

  • GLP-1 receptor agonists (true incretin mimetics):

    • Exenatide

    • Liraglutide

  • Metformin → ↓ hepatic gluconeogenesis

Exam Pearl:
Oral incretin-based antidiabetic drug = Sitagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫৭) Which insulin preparation is long acting?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Insulin glargine is a long-acting basal insulin analogue with a prolonged, relatively peakless action profile lasting about 24 hours or longer. It provides continuous insulin coverage and is commonly used for basal insulin replacement in diabetes management. Aspart is a rapid-acting insulin analogue, isophane (NPH insulin) is an intermediate-acting insulin, and Ultralente is a long-acting insulin preparation but is rarely used today. In modern clinical practice and exam settings, glargine is the preferred answer for long-acting insulin.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Rapid acting:

    • Aspart

    • Lispro

    • Glulisine

  • Intermediate acting:

    • Isophane (NPH)

  • Long acting:

    • Glargine

    • Detemir

    • Degludec

  • Glargine → peakless basal insulin

Exam Pearl:
Long-acting insulin analogue commonly tested = Insulin glargine.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫৮) Air Bronchogram in CXR is found in….?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
An air bronchogram on chest X-ray is classically seen in lung consolidation. It occurs when the alveoli become filled with fluid, pus, blood, or cells, while the air-filled bronchi remain patent. The air within the bronchi appears as visible branching dark lines against the opaque consolidated lung. It is commonly seen in lobar pneumonia.

In pleural effusion, the lung is compressed and air bronchograms are usually absent. Mass lesions and collapse (atelectasis) may rarely show air bronchograms, but consolidation is the classic and most common association.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Air bronchogram → Consolidation

  • Common cause → Pneumonia

  • Mechanism:

    • Alveoli filled with fluid/pus

    • Bronchi remain air-filled

  • Pleural effusion → meniscus sign

  • Atelectasis → volume loss + mediastinal shift toward affected side

Exam Pearl:
Visible air-filled bronchi within an opaque lung field = air bronchogram = consolidation.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৫৯) A patient receiving carbimazole comes to you with sore throat. What may be the reason?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
A patient taking carbimazole who develops sore throat should be suspected of having agranulocytosis, a rare but serious adverse effect of antithyroid drugs. Carbimazole can cause severe reduction of neutrophils, leading to increased susceptibility to infections, often presenting with fever and sore throat due to oropharyngeal infection. Immediate withdrawal of the drug and urgent full blood count (FBC) with neutrophil count assessment are required. Hypersensitivity reactions may occur but are not the classic exam association with sore throat.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Carbimazole adverse effects:

    • Agranulocytosis → fever + sore throat

    • Rash

    • Hepatotoxicity (rare)

  • Antithyroid drugs:

    • Carbimazole

    • Methimazole

    • Propylthiouracil (PTU)

  • Agranulocytosis → ↓ neutrophils → infection risk

Exam Pearl:
Sore throat in a patient on carbimazole = suspect agranulocytosis until proven otherwise.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬০) What is the recommended % of energy intake from fat in a diabetic patient?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
In a diabetic patient, dietary fat intake should generally be less than 35% of total daily energy intake. The aim is to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease, which is a major complication of diabetes. Saturated fat should be limited further (usually <10% of total energy) and replaced with unsaturated fats. A very high-fat diet can worsen insulin resistance and dyslipidemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Diabetes diet composition:

    • Fat → <35% of total energy

    • Saturated fat → <10%

    • Protein → about 15–20%

    • Carbohydrate → individualized (usually 45–60%)

  • Avoid:

    • Trans fats

    • Excess saturated fats

Exam Pearl:
Recommended fat intake in diabetes = less than 35% of total energy.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬১) Which is the main drug used in bipolar disorder?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Lithium is considered the main and classic mood stabilizer used in the treatment of bipolar disorder, especially for the prevention of manic and depressive episodes and maintenance therapy. It is particularly effective in reducing the risk of suicide in bipolar patients.

Olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone are atypical antipsychotics that are also used in bipolar disorder, especially for acute mania and as adjunctive therapy, but they are not the primary classic mood stabilizer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • First-line mood stabilizer → Lithium

  • Lithium uses:

    • Bipolar disorder (maintenance)

    • Acute mania

    • Suicide risk reduction

  • Lithium adverse effects:

    • Tremor

    • Hypothyroidism

    • Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

    • Ebstein anomaly (pregnancy)

Exam Pearl:
Classic main drug for bipolar disorder = Lithium.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬২) Which is the most common cause of dementia?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Alzheimer’s disease is the most common cause of dementia worldwide. It is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by accumulation of β-amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles (tau protein), leading to neuronal loss and cognitive decline. It typically presents with progressive memory impairment, followed by deterioration of language, judgment, and daily functioning.

Cerebral tumors, multiple sclerosis, and thiamine deficiency (e.g., Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome) can cause cognitive impairment but are much less common causes of dementia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common dementia → Alzheimer’s disease

  • Pathology:

    • β-amyloid plaques

    • Neurofibrillary tangles (tau)

  • Other causes:

    • Vascular dementia

    • Lewy body dementia

    • Frontotemporal dementia

  • Thiamine deficiency → Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome

Exam Pearl:
Progressive dementia in elderly patients = Alzheimer’s disease until proven otherwise.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬৩) In Budd-Chiari syndrome, where thrombosis occurs?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Budd–Chiari syndrome occurs due to thrombosis or obstruction of the hepatic veins (and sometimes the hepatic portion of the inferior vena cava), causing impaired hepatic venous outflow. This leads to congestion of the liver, resulting in tender hepatomegaly, abdominal pain, and ascites.

Portal vein thrombosis causes portal hypertension but is not Budd–Chiari syndrome. Central vein and cystic vein thrombosis are not associated with this condition.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Budd–Chiari syndrome → Hepatic vein thrombosis

  • Pathophysiology:

    • ↓ Hepatic venous drainage

    • ↑ Sinusoidal pressure

    • Congestive hepatomegaly

    • Ascites

  • Risk factors:

    • Myeloproliferative disorders

    • Hypercoagulable states

    • Pregnancy/OCP use

Exam Pearl:
Budd–Chiari = blockage of hepatic veins → hepatic outflow obstruction.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬৪) The term 'Anhedonia' that occurs in depressive disorder means.....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Anhedonia means loss of the ability to experience pleasure or enjoyment from activities that were previously enjoyable. It is one of the core symptoms of depressive disorder and is commonly seen along with depressed mood.

Although loss of interest (apathy) is closely related, the precise definition of anhedonia is loss of enjoyment/pleasure. Reduced self-esteem and depressed mood are other symptoms of depression but do not define anhedonia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anhedonia → Loss of pleasure/enjoyment

  • Core symptoms of depression:

    • Depressed mood

    • Anhedonia

    • Reduced energy/fatigue

  • Other depressive features:

    • Low self-esteem

    • Sleep disturbance

    • Appetite change

    • Suicidal thoughts

Exam Pearl:
Anhedonia = inability to feel pleasure (loss of enjoyment).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬৫) Which one is 1st line drug for focal seizure?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The first-line drug for focal (partial) seizures is commonly Levetiracetam (also Lamotrigine is an accepted first-line option in many guidelines). Levetiracetam is widely used because of its broad spectrum of activity, good tolerability, few drug interactions, and safety profile.

Sodium valproate is mainly used for generalized seizures and is not preferred as first-line therapy for focal seizures due to adverse effects. Ethosuximide is specifically used for absence seizures, not focal seizures.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Focal seizure → Levetiracetam / Lamotrigine

  • Generalized tonic-clonic seizure → Valproate, Lamotrigine, Levetiracetam

  • Absence seizure → Ethosuximide

  • Levetiracetam:

    • Few drug interactions

    • Acts via SV2A synaptic vesicle protein

Exam Pearl:
Common first-line drug for focal seizures = Levetiracetam.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬৬) Which investigation is more sensitive in detecting early abnormalities of encephalitis?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
MRI brain is the most sensitive investigation for detecting early abnormalities in encephalitis, especially viral encephalitis. MRI can demonstrate early inflammatory changes, particularly in the temporal lobes in Herpes simplex encephalitis (HSE), before abnormalities become apparent on CT.

EEG may show supportive findings (e.g., periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges in HSV encephalitis) but is not as sensitive for structural changes. CT may be normal in early disease, and MRA evaluates cerebral blood vessels rather than brain inflammation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Early encephalitis detection → MRI brain

  • HSV encephalitis:

    • Affects temporal lobes

    • MRI → temporal lobe hyperintensity

  • CSF examination:

    • Lymphocytic pleocytosis

    • ↑ Protein

    • Normal glucose

Exam Pearl:
MRI is the most sensitive imaging modality for early encephalitis changes.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬৭) Which type of psoriasis is most common in children & adolescent?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Guttate psoriasis is the most common type of psoriasis in children and adolescents. It typically presents as multiple small, drop-shaped erythematous scaly lesions on the trunk and proximal limbs. It is often triggered by a recent Streptococcus pyogenes infection, especially pharyngitis.

Plaque psoriasis is the most common type of psoriasis overall in adults, characterized by well-demarcated thick plaques with silvery scales. Pustular and erythrodermic psoriasis are uncommon and more severe forms.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Children/adolescents → Guttate psoriasis

  • Trigger → Streptococcal throat infection

  • Lesions → Small “drop-like” scaly papules

  • Most common psoriasis overall → Plaque psoriasis

Exam Pearl:
Young patient + sudden small teardrop lesions after sore throat = Guttate psoriasis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬৮) Gram negative diplococci in microscopy is suggestive of which disease?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Gram-negative diplococci seen on microscopy are characteristic of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, the causative organism of gonorrhea. They are typically seen as kidney-shaped diplococci inside neutrophils in a urethral discharge smear.

Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum (a spirochete), AIDS is caused by HIV, and chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi (Gram-negative coccobacillus).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gonorrhea → Neisseria gonorrhoeae

  • Microscopy:

    • Gram-negative diplococci

    • Intracellular in neutrophils

  • Syphilis → Treponema pallidum

  • Chancroid → Haemophilus ducreyi

Exam Pearl:
Intracellular Gram-negative diplococci = Gonorrhea.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৬৯) Which is not a features of Klinefelter's syndrome?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is a chromosomal disorder affecting males. It is characterized by phenotypic male appearance, testicular atrophy, infertility due to impaired spermatogenesis, and gynecomastia due to an increased estrogen-to-androgen ratio.

Webbed neck is not a feature of Klinefelter syndrome; it is classically associated with Turner syndrome (45,X).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Klinefelter syndrome → 47,XXY

    • Male phenotype

    • Tall stature

    • Small firm testes

    • Infertility

    • Gynecomastia

  • Turner syndrome → 45,X

    • Female phenotype

    • Webbed neck

    • Short stature

    • Coarctation of aorta

Exam Pearl:
Webbed neck = Turner syndrome, not Klinefelter syndrome.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭০) Which is contraindication of colonoscopy?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) is a contraindication for colonoscopy because full colonoscopy carries a high risk of colonic perforation and toxic megacolon due to severe inflammation and fragile bowel wall. In such cases, limited flexible sigmoidoscopy is preferred for assessment.

Colonoscopy is commonly indicated in suspected IBD, chronic diarrhoea, and colorectal carcinoma for diagnosis, biopsy, and evaluation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Colonoscopy contraindication:

    • Acute severe colitis (risk of perforation)

    • Toxic megacolon

    • Suspected bowel perforation

  • Colonoscopy indications:

    • Suspected IBD

    • Chronic diarrhoea evaluation

    • Colorectal cancer screening/diagnosis

Exam Pearl:
Avoid full colonoscopy in acute severe ulcerative colitis; use flexible sigmoidoscopy instead.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭১) Which has revolutionized the treatment of moderate to severe acne?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Isotretinoin has revolutionized the treatment of moderate to severe acne, especially severe nodulocystic acne and acne resistant to conventional therapy. It is an oral retinoid that acts on all major pathogenic factors of acne by reducing sebaceous gland activity, decreasing sebum production, normalizing follicular keratinization, and reducing Cutibacterium acnes colonization.

Benzoyl peroxide and topical retinoids are useful for mild to moderate acne, while OCPs may help in hormonally mediated acne in females but are not the main treatment for severe acne.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Severe acne → Oral isotretinoin

  • Mechanism:

    • ↓ Sebum production

    • ↓ Sebaceous gland size

    • ↓ Comedone formation

    • Anti-inflammatory effect

  • Major adverse effects:

    • Teratogenicity

    • Dry skin/lips

    • ↑ Liver enzymes & lipids

Exam Pearl:
Isotretinoin = breakthrough drug for moderate to severe acne.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭২) Water lily sign is pathognomonic for…?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The water lily sign is a classic radiological finding of a hydatid cyst caused by Echinococcus granulosus. It occurs when the endocyst (detached germinal membrane) separates from the pericyst and floats within the cyst fluid, resembling a floating water lily. It is considered a characteristic/pathognomonic sign of a hydatid cyst, especially in the liver.

Amoebic and pyogenic liver abscesses may show cavity formation but do not produce the water lily sign. HCC is a malignant liver tumor and has different imaging features.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Water lily sign → Hydatid cyst

  • Cause → Echinococcus granulosus

  • Common site → Liver

  • Other hydatid signs:

    • Daughter cysts

    • Detached membrane sign

Exam Pearl:
Floating membrane inside cyst = Water lily sign = Hydatid disease.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭৩) Which is the single best test to confirm iron deficiency?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Serum (plasma) ferritin is the single best test to confirm iron deficiency because it reflects the body's iron stores. A low ferritin level is highly specific for iron deficiency anemia (IDA).

In iron deficiency:

  • Serum iron ↓

  • TIBC ↑

  • Transferrin ↑

  • Ferritin ↓ (best indicator of depleted iron stores)

However, ferritin is an acute-phase reactant and may be falsely elevated in infection, inflammation, liver disease, or malignancy.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Best test for iron deficiency → Serum ferritin

  • Iron deficiency anemia profile:

    • Ferritin ↓

    • Serum iron ↓

    • TIBC ↑

    • Transferrin saturation ↓

  • Anemia of chronic disease:

    • Ferritin ↑/normal

    • TIBC ↓

Exam Pearl:
Low serum ferritin = most specific evidence of iron deficiency.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭৪) Philadelphia chromosomes is associated with which type of leukemia?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The Philadelphia chromosome (t(9;22)) is classically associated with Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). It results from a reciprocal translocation between chromosome 9 and chromosome 22, creating the BCR-ABL fusion gene, which produces a constitutively active tyrosine kinase that promotes uncontrolled proliferation of myeloid cells.

Although the Philadelphia chromosome can also be seen in some cases of ALL (especially adult B-cell ALL), the classic and most common association is CML.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Philadelphia chromosome → CML

  • Genetic abnormality:

    • t(9;22)

    • BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase

  • CML marker:

    • ↑ WBC with granulocytic proliferation

    • Splenomegaly

    • Low leukocyte alkaline phosphatase (LAP)

Exam Pearl:
t(9;22) + BCR-ABL = Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭৫) Which drug is used in 1st line treatment of multiple myeloma?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Bortezomib is one of the key first-line drugs used in the treatment of multiple myeloma. It is a proteasome inhibitor that causes accumulation of abnormal proteins within plasma cells, leading to plasma cell apoptosis. Modern first-line regimens commonly include bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (VRd regimen).

Melphalan was historically used in multiple myeloma, especially with steroids, but is less commonly used as initial therapy in many current regimens. Prednisolone may be used as part of combination therapy, while imatinib is used mainly for CML with BCR-ABL positivity.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Multiple myeloma → Bortezomib (proteasome inhibitor)

  • Diagnostic features (CRAB):

    • Calcium ↑

    • Renal impairment

    • Anemia

    • Bone lesions

  • Other drugs:

    • Lenalidomide → immunomodulatory drug

    • Dexamethasone → combination therapy

Exam Pearl:
First-line targeted therapy in multiple myeloma = Bortezomib.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭৬) Which disease is characterized by Auspitz sign?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Auspitz sign is a classic feature of psoriasis. It is the appearance of pinpoint bleeding spots when psoriatic scales are scraped off, due to exposure of dilated capillaries in the dermal papillae. It occurs because of thinning of the epidermis overlying these capillaries.

Scabies, eczema, and taeniasis are not associated with Auspitz sign.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Auspitz sign → Psoriasis

  • Psoriasis features:

    • Well-demarcated erythematous plaques

    • Silvery scales

    • Auspitz sign

    • Koebner phenomenon

  • Common sites:

    • Extensor surfaces

    • Scalp

    • Lumbosacral region

Exam Pearl:
Auspitz sign = pinpoint bleeding after scraping scales = Psoriasis.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭৭) What is a major cause of disability & suicide?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Depression (major depressive disorder) is a major cause of disability worldwide and is strongly associated with suicide risk. It causes persistent low mood, loss of interest (anhedonia), impaired functioning, sleep and appetite disturbances, and feelings of hopelessness.

Mania occurs in bipolar disorder but is not the leading cause of disability and suicide. Dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder) is a chronic but usually milder form of depression. Anxiety disorders can cause significant impairment but are less strongly associated with suicide compared with major depression.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Major cause of disability + suicide → Depression

  • Core symptoms:

    • Depressed mood

    • Anhedonia

    • Low energy

    • Hopelessness

    • Suicidal thoughts

  • Bipolar disorder:

    • Mania + depression episodes

Exam Pearl:
Depression is one of the leading causes of disability and the most important psychiatric risk factor for suicide.
