Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭৮) 'Excessive fear of dying in an air crash leading to avoidance of flying' - is......?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Excessive, irrational fear of a specific object or situation (such as fear of flying, heights, animals, or enclosed spaces) leading to avoidance behavior is characteristic of a phobic disorder (specific phobia).

Fear of dying in an air crash and avoiding flying is a classic example of specific situational phobia (aviophobia).

Panic disorder involves recurrent unexpected panic attacks, while generalized anxiety disorder involves excessive worry about multiple areas of life. Depression is not primarily characterized by specific fear and avoidance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Specific phobia → excessive fear + avoidance of specific stimulus

  • Examples:

    • Flying

    • Heights

    • Animals

    • Blood/injury

  • Panic disorder → recurrent unexpected panic attacks

  • GAD → excessive worry for ≥6 months

Exam Pearl:
Fear of a specific situation causing avoidance = Phobic disorder.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৭৯) Which side effect is most common in H. pylori eradication therapy?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The most common side effect of H. pylori eradication therapy is diarrhoea. This occurs mainly due to the use of antibiotics (especially clarithromycin, amoxicillin, and metronidazole) which alter the normal intestinal flora.

Standard eradication regimens include a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) + two antibiotics, and gastrointestinal adverse effects are common. Nausea, abdominal discomfort, and taste disturbance may also occur, but diarrhoea is the most frequently reported adverse effect.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • H. pylori eradication therapy:

    • PPI + antibiotics

    • Common side effect → Diarrhoea

  • Clarithromycin → metallic taste

  • Metronidazole → metallic taste, disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol

  • Antibiotics → gut flora disturbance → diarrhoea

Exam Pearl:
H. pylori treatment + antibiotic use = most common adverse effect is diarrhoea.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮০) The triad of hyponatremia, hemodilution & urine hypertonic of plasma suggest diagnosis of….?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The triad of hyponatremia, hemodilution, and urine hypertonic compared with plasma is characteristic of Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH).

In SIADH, excessive secretion of ADH (vasopressin) causes increased water reabsorption in the kidneys, leading to:

  • Dilutional hyponatremia

  • Reduced plasma osmolality (hypotonic plasma)

  • Inappropriately concentrated urine (urine osmolality higher than plasma)

Diabetes insipidus causes the opposite picture: excessive dilute urine and hypernatremia. Conn’s syndrome causes hyperaldosteronism with hypertension and hypokalemia. Cushing’s syndrome causes cortisol excess.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • SIADH:

    • Na⁺ ↓

    • Plasma osmolality ↓

    • Urine osmolality ↑

    • Euvolemic state

  • Causes:

    • Small cell lung carcinoma

    • CNS disorders

    • Drugs (e.g., carbamazepine)

Exam Pearl:
Hyponatremia + concentrated urine despite low plasma osmolality = SIADH.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮১) Which is not an X-ray finding of mitral stenosis?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Oligemic lung field is not a feature of mitral stenosis. Mitral stenosis causes obstruction of blood flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle, leading to left atrial enlargement and pulmonary venous hypertension. This results in pulmonary congestion, not reduced pulmonary vascularity.

Typical X-ray findings of mitral stenosis include:

  • Double-contour right heart border → due to enlarged left atrium

  • Mitral valve calcification (in long-standing disease)

  • Pulmonary venous hypertension → upper lobe diversion, pulmonary edema

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Mitral stenosis X-ray:

    • Left atrial enlargement

    • Straightening of left heart border

    • Double density sign

    • Pulmonary venous hypertension

    • Mitral valve calcification

  • Oligemic lung fields → seen in conditions with reduced pulmonary blood flow (e.g., TOF)

Exam Pearl:
Mitral stenosis causes pulmonary congestion, not oligemia.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮২) Which component of vitamin B complex doesn't show neurological manifestation?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Among the given vitamin B complex components, riboflavin (vitamin B2) is the one that does not typically cause neurological manifestations. Its deficiency mainly causes mucocutaneous features such as cheilosis, angular stomatitis, glossitis, and dermatitis.

Other options have important neurological associations:

  • Thiamine (B1) → Wernicke encephalopathy, Korsakoff syndrome, peripheral neuropathy

  • Niacin (B3) → Pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia)

  • Pyridoxine (B6) → peripheral neuropathy (especially with isoniazid therapy)

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • B1 deficiency → Wernicke-Korsakoff + neuropathy

  • B2 deficiency → Cheilosis, glossitis, dermatitis

  • B3 deficiency → Pellagra (3 D’s)

  • B6 deficiency → Peripheral neuropathy, seizures

Exam Pearl:
Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency is mainly mucocutaneous, not neurological.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮৩) Which Bariatric surgery is most effective in weight reduction?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Among bariatric surgeries, Duodenal switch (biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch) produces the greatest weight reduction and has the highest metabolic effect. It combines a restrictive component (sleeve gastrectomy) with a strong malabsorptive component, resulting in significant and sustained weight loss.

Roux-en-Y gastric bypass is also highly effective and is one of the most commonly performed bariatric procedures, but it produces less weight loss compared with duodenal switch. Gastric banding has the least weight reduction among these options.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Maximum weight loss → Duodenal switch

  • Roux-en-Y gastric bypass:

    • Restrictive + mild malabsorptive

    • Commonly performed

  • Sleeve gastrectomy:

    • Restrictive only

  • Gastric banding:

    • Least effective weight loss

Exam Pearl:
Most effective bariatric surgery for weight reduction = Duodenal switch.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮৪) What is the nature of percussion note in pneumonia?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
In pneumonia, the affected lung area undergoes consolidation, where alveoli become filled with inflammatory exudate instead of air. This increased tissue density produces a dull percussion note on examination.

  • Resonant → normal lung

  • Woody dull → classically described in massive pleural effusion

  • Stony dull → pleural effusion (especially fluid in pleural cavity)

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Lung consolidation (pneumonia) → Dull percussion note

  • Pleural effusion → Stony dull

  • Pneumothorax → Hyper-resonant

  • Normal lung → Resonant

Exam Pearl:
Pneumonia causes consolidation → consolidation gives a dull percussion note.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮৫) Passage of fresh blood in stool is called....?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Hematochezia refers to the passage of fresh, bright red blood per rectum, usually mixed with or coating the stool. It commonly indicates lower gastrointestinal bleeding, such as from hemorrhoids, anal fissure, diverticular disease, or colorectal carcinoma.

  • Hematemesis → vomiting of blood (upper GI bleeding)

  • Melena → black, tarry stool due to digested blood, usually from upper GI bleeding

  • Hemophilia → inherited bleeding disorder, not a type of stool bleeding

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hematochezia → Fresh red blood in stool

  • Melena → Black tarry stool

  • Hematemesis → Blood vomiting

  • Lower GI bleeding → usually hematochezia

Exam Pearl:
Fresh blood per rectum = Hematochezia.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮৬) Which one is a feature of Type-1 DM?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.option2: History of other autoimmune disease common
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Type-1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is an autoimmune disease caused by destruction of pancreatic β-cells, leading to absolute insulin deficiency. Therefore, patients with Type-1 DM commonly have a history of other autoimmune disorders, such as autoimmune thyroid disease, coeliac disease, and Addison’s disease.

Other options are incorrect:

  • Family history common → more typical of Type-2 DM (though genetic predisposition exists in T1DM).

  • Usually obese → Type-2 DM is commonly associated with obesity.

  • Usually occurs after 50 years → Type-2 DM usually occurs in older adults.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Type-1 DM:

    • Autoimmune β-cell destruction

    • Young age onset (commonly childhood/adolescence)

    • Low/absent C-peptide

    • Requires insulin therapy

    • Associated with other autoimmune diseases

  • Type-2 DM:

    • Insulin resistance

    • Obesity association

    • Strong family history

Exam Pearl:
Type-1 DM + other autoimmune disease association = autoimmune β-cell destruction.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮৭) Which is the feature of hypoglycemic coma?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Hypoglycemic coma occurs due to severe reduction in blood glucose causing neuroglycopenia and autonomic activation. Severe hypoglycemia may present with features of shock-like states, including sweating, tachycardia, hypotension, and altered consciousness progressing to coma.

Other options are less typical:

  • Abdominal pain → not a feature of hypoglycemic coma.

  • Bounding pulse → not characteristic (hypoglycemia usually causes tachycardia with sympathetic activation, not bounding pulse).

  • Blurring of vision → may occur in hypoglycemia but is not the key feature of coma.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypoglycemia symptoms:

    • Sweating

    • Tremor

    • Palpitations

    • Hunger

    • Confusion

    • Seizure/coma

  • Severe hypoglycemia → neuroglycopenia → loss of consciousness

Exam Pearl:
Severe hypoglycemia can present with shock-like features and coma.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮৮) Which is a feature of autonomic neuropathy in diabetic patient?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Gustatory sweating is a feature of diabetic autonomic neuropathy. It occurs due to abnormal sympathetic nerve regeneration affecting sweat glands, causing profuse sweating over the face and neck during eating.

Other options are features of different diabetic neuropathies:

  • Ocular palsies → diabetic cranial mononeuropathy (especially CN III palsy)

  • Amyotrophy → diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy

  • Carpal tunnel syndrome → entrapment neuropathy associated with diabetes

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Diabetic autonomic neuropathy:

    • Gastroparesis

    • Postural hypotension

    • Resting tachycardia

    • Bladder dysfunction

    • Erectile dysfunction

    • Gustatory sweating

  • Peripheral neuropathy → stocking-glove sensory loss

Exam Pearl:
Sweating during meals in diabetes = gustatory sweating → autonomic neuropathy.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৮৯) Toxicity of which drug causes hepatorenal failure?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Narcotic drug toxicity can cause severe systemic complications, including hepatorenal failure, especially with prolonged use or overdose of certain opioids due to hypoxia, toxic metabolites, and associated organ injury.

Among the options:

  • ACE inhibitors → may cause renal impairment (especially in renal artery stenosis) but not typical hepatic failure.

  • Anxiolytics → mainly cause CNS depression; not associated with hepatorenal failure.

  • Codeine is a narcotic opioid, so it falls under the narcotics group.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Opioid toxicity:

    • CNS depression

    • Respiratory depression

    • Miosis

    • Possible organ injury in severe toxicity

  • Paracetamol toxicity (not listed) is the classic cause of acute hepatic failure.

Exam Pearl:
Among the given choices, narcotics toxicity is the best answer; paracetamol is the classic drug causing acute liver failure.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯০) What is the single most important investigation in hypothyroidism?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The single most important investigation in hypothyroidism is serum TSH. It is the most sensitive screening test for primary hypothyroidism because even a small reduction in thyroid hormone levels causes a compensatory rise in pituitary TSH secretion.

In primary hypothyroidism:

  • TSH ↑

  • Free T4 ↓

FT4 helps assess the severity and confirm the diagnosis, but TSH is the best initial test. FT3 is not useful because it may remain normal in hypothyroidism. Thyroid scan is not routinely required for diagnosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Primary hypothyroidism:

    • TSH ↑

    • FT4 ↓

  • Secondary hypothyroidism:

    • TSH ↓/normal

    • FT4 ↓

  • Most sensitive screening test → Serum TSH

Exam Pearl:
Suspected hypothyroidism → first investigation = Serum TSH.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯১) Which is the commonest metabolic bone disease?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Osteoporosis is the commonest metabolic bone disease worldwide. It is characterized by reduced bone mass and deterioration of bone microarchitecture, leading to increased risk of fragility fractures, especially of the hip, vertebrae, and wrist.

  • Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease, not a metabolic bone disease.

  • Osteomalacia occurs due to defective mineralization of adult bone, commonly from vitamin D deficiency.

  • Rickets is the childhood counterpart of osteomalacia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common metabolic bone disease → Osteoporosis

  • Osteoporosis:

    • ↓ Bone mineral density

    • Normal mineralization

    • Fragility fractures

  • Osteomalacia:

    • Defective mineralization

    • Vitamin D deficiency

  • Rickets:

    • Childhood osteomalacia

Exam Pearl:
Osteoporosis = most common metabolic bone disease.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯২) ‘0nion skin spleen’ is classically found in which disease?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
“Onion skin spleen” is a classic histopathological finding associated with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). It refers to concentric fibrosis around splenic arteries (periarterial fibrosis), giving an appearance similar to layers of an onion.

Other options:

  • Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) → may cause rheumatoid nodules and splenomegaly (Felty syndrome), but not onion skin spleen.

  • AIDS → associated with opportunistic infections and lymphoid changes.

  • Lymphoma → may involve spleen but does not produce onion skin appearance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Onion skin spleen → SLE

  • SLE pathology:

    • Hematoxylin bodies

    • LE cells

    • Wire-loop lesions in lupus nephritis

    • Onion skin periarterial fibrosis in spleen

Exam Pearl:
Concentric periarterial fibrosis of spleen (“onion skin”) = SLE.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯৩) What is the commonest cause of coma in DM?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The commonest cause of coma in a diabetic patient is hypoglycemia, especially due to excess insulin or antidiabetic drug therapy. Severe hypoglycemia causes neuroglycopenia, leading to confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness, and coma.

Although DKA and HHS can cause diabetic coma, they are less common causes compared with hypoglycemia in clinical practice. Lactic acidosis is a rare complication, mainly associated with metformin use in predisposed patients.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common cause of diabetic coma → Hypoglycemia

  • Hypoglycemia features:

    • Sweating

    • Tremor

    • Palpitations

    • Confusion

    • Seizure/coma

  • DKA:

    • Type 1 DM

    • Ketosis + metabolic acidosis

  • HHS:

    • Type 2 DM

    • Severe hyperglycemia + dehydration

Exam Pearl:
In a diabetic patient with coma, always consider hypoglycemia first.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯৪) Which of the following condition is characterized by short stature?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Turner syndrome (45,X) is classically characterized by short stature due to loss of one X chromosome causing impaired growth. Other features include webbed neck, shield chest, ovarian dysgenesis, primary amenorrhea, and coarctation of the aorta.

Other options:

  • Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) → usually tall stature, small testes, infertility, gynecomastia.

  • Marfan syndrome → tall, long limbs (marfanoid habitus).

  • Homocystinuria → tall stature with long limbs, lens dislocation, and thromboembolism.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Turner syndrome → Short female + 45,X

  • Klinefelter → Tall male + 47,XXY

  • Marfan → Tall, arachnodactyly, ectopia lentis

  • Homocystinuria → Tall, downward lens dislocation

Exam Pearl:
Short stature in a chromosomal disorder = Turner syndrome.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯৫) What is the 1st line treatment of predominant hypertriglyceridemia?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
For predominant hypertriglyceridemia, the first-line drug treatment is a fibrate (e.g., fenofibrate, gemfibrozil). Fibrates activate PPAR-α receptors, which increase lipoprotein lipase activity and enhance triglyceride clearance, producing a significant reduction in triglyceride levels.

  • Statins are first-line for predominant LDL cholesterol elevation.

  • Ezetimibe mainly reduces LDL cholesterol by inhibiting intestinal cholesterol absorption.

  • Resins (bile acid sequestrants) reduce LDL but may increase triglycerides, so they are avoided in hypertriglyceridemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ↑ Triglycerides → Fibrate

  • ↑ LDL cholesterol → Statin

  • Severe TG elevation (>500 mg/dL):

    • Risk of pancreatitis

    • Fibrate + lifestyle modification

  • Fibrate adverse effect:

    • Myopathy (especially with statins)

    • Gallstones

Exam Pearl:
Predominant hypertriglyceridemia = treat with fibrates (first-line).

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯৬) What is the target BP of a diabetic patient without proteinuria?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
The recommended target blood pressure in a diabetic patient without proteinuria is <130/80 mmHg (commonly used exam answer: 130/80 mmHg). Strict BP control in diabetes reduces the risk of cardiovascular complications and microvascular complications.

In diabetic patients with proteinuria/albuminuria, some guidelines may recommend a lower target (around <130/80 mmHg, depending on individual risk and guideline).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Diabetes without proteinuria → BP target ≈ 130/80 mmHg

  • Hypertension in diabetes increases risk of:

    • Nephropathy

    • Retinopathy

    • Cardiovascular disease

  • ACE inhibitors/ARBs are preferred when:

    • Albuminuria/proteinuria present

Exam Pearl:
Diabetic patient BP goal = around 130/80 mmHg.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯৭) Which is a contraindication of stomach wash?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Kerosene (hydrocarbon) poisoning is a contraindication for gastric lavage (stomach wash) because it has a high risk of aspiration into the lungs, leading to chemical pneumonitis. Gastric lavage can increase this risk.

Gastric lavage may be considered in selected cases of severe poisoning (within an appropriate time window and with airway protection), such as:

  • Aspirin poisoning

  • Paracetamol poisoning

  • Some other toxic ingestions

Arsenic poisoning may also require specific management, but it is not the classic contraindication among the given options.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Contraindication of gastric lavage:

    • Hydrocarbon poisoning (kerosene, petrol)

    • Corrosive ingestion (acid/alkali)

    • Unprotected airway

  • Kerosene poisoning → aspiration → chemical pneumonitis

Exam Pearl:
Never do gastric lavage in kerosene poisoning due to aspiration risk.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯৮) Which is non specific sign of anemia?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Pallor is a non-specific sign of anemia. It occurs due to reduced hemoglobin concentration causing decreased redness of the skin and mucous membranes. However, pallor can also be seen in many other conditions (e.g., shock, vasoconstriction, chronic illness), so it is not specific for anemia.

Other options are common symptoms of anemia:

  • Tiredness → due to reduced oxygen delivery to tissues

  • Breathlessness → compensatory response to tissue hypoxia

  • Lightheadedness → due to reduced cerebral oxygenation

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Symptoms of anemia:

    • Fatigue

    • Dyspnea

    • Dizziness/lightheadedness

    • Palpitations

  • Signs:

    • Pallor (non-specific)

    • Tachycardia

    • Flow murmur

Exam Pearl:
Pallor is a classic but non-specific sign of anemia.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ৯৯) Which is hypokinetic disorder?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Catatonia is a hypokinetic movement disorder characterized by reduced or absent voluntary movements, including stupor, immobility, mutism, and posturing. It is commonly associated with psychiatric disorders (especially schizophrenia and mood disorders) and some medical conditions.

Other options are hyperkinetic disorders:

  • Tremor → rhythmic involuntary movements

  • Chorea → irregular, rapid, jerky movements

  • Tics → repetitive, sudden, involuntary movements or vocalizations

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypokinetic disorders:

    • Parkinsonism

    • Catatonia

    • Bradykinesia/akinesia

  • Hyperkinetic disorders:

    • Tremor

    • Chorea

    • Tics

    • Dystonia

Exam Pearl:
Reduced movement + immobility = hypokinetic disorder → Catatonia.

Subject Final-05 Medicine.question: ১০০) What type of drug 'Terbinafine' is?
Subject Final-05 Medicine.exp:
Terbinafine is an antifungal drug belonging to the class allylamines. It is particularly effective against dermatophyte infections (tinea infections) involving the skin, hair, and nails.

It works by inhibiting squalene epoxidase, an enzyme involved in ergosterol synthesis in fungal cell membranes, leading to accumulation of toxic squalene and fungal cell death.

Other options:

  • Antibacterial → acts against bacteria (e.g., penicillins)

  • Antiviral → acts against viruses (e.g., acyclovir)

  • Antiprotozoal → acts against protozoa (e.g., metronidazole)

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Terbinafine → Allylamine antifungal

  • Mechanism → ↓ Squalene epoxidase → ↓ Ergosterol synthesis

  • Uses:

    • Tinea pedis

    • Tinea corporis

    • Onychomycosis (fungal nail infection)

Exam Pearl:
Terbinafine = antifungal drug used mainly for dermatophyte infections.
